clue.text: Draw untidy Wombles and die!

indicators.note: untidy says the letters of the two words lie in a mess, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A command to scruffy furry TV creatures, the Wombles, to perish.
explanation.walkthrough: The Wombles are litter-picking furry creatures from a British children's TV show. 'Draw' is the old sense of disembowelling a condemned person, as in hanged, drawn and quartered.
explanation.definitionFit: To draw a carcass or a traitor is to remove the entrails, an old synonym.

clue.text: Name of mountains giving a warning to mice?

definitions.text: Name of mountains giving a warning to mice?

parts.words: Name of mountains giving a warning to mice?
parts.note: the name of a New York range, split in two, reads as what a feline does to rodents: a mouse's warning of a pet's slaughter

explanation.surface: A whimsical question about which mountain range sounds like a threat to rodents.
explanation.definitionFit: The range in New York State whose name splits into a feline's possessive and a word for slaughter.

clue.text: Knockout kiss in a Russian's purse?

definitions.note: describes a thing found in a Russian's purse, a noun

parts.note: KO is the boxing abbreviation for a knockout
a peck is a quick light kiss

explanation.surface: A stunning kiss stashed in a Russian handbag.
explanation.definitionFit: A small Russian coin, a hundredth of a rouble, is just what a Russian's purse might hold.

clue.text: On the radio something blue will usually move a square?

definitions.note: describes a chess piece by its typical move of one square, standing for a noun

indicators.note: something heard on the radio is spoken, so a word is replaced by one sounding the same

parts.note: blue means smutty, and porn is something blue

explanation.surface: A coy question about something risqué being broadcast and nudging an old-fashioned person.
explanation.walkthrough: In non-rhotic British speech the two words sound identical. 'Square' looks like a fogey; here it is a chessboard square.
explanation.definitionFit: The chess foot soldier normally advances a single square at a time.

clue.text: Say it aloud, sending ships to the Gulf was such a mistake — a build-up demanding contemplation

indicators.note: the instruction to speak tells us the phrase is replaced by one sounding the same

parts.words: sending ships to the Gulf was such a mistake
parts.note: a mistake involving warships is a naval fluff, fluff being a blunder

explanation.surface: A political jibe about a misguided naval deployment to the Persian Gulf.
explanation.walkthrough: Fluff is a blunder; a naval one would be sending the fleet in error. The lint that builds up in a belly button is what navel-gazers contemplate.
explanation.definitionFit: Lint gathering in a belly button, the spot people stare at in navel-gazing contemplation.

clue.text: Anti the mission for military subjugation

parts.note: con means against, as in pros and cons
a quest is a mission or expedition

explanation.surface: Opposition to the mission that aims at military domination.
explanation.definitionFit: Subduing a land by force of arms is its conquest, a synonym.

clue.text: Girl, one snared by parasite

indicators.note: something snared by another is caught inside it

parts.note: a louse is a parasitic insect
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A girl, one caught by a hanger-on.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's given name, so a girl may be called this.

clue.text: Pine for actor

definitions.meaning: a pine is a kind of conifer
Herbert Beerbohm ... was a celebrated Victorian actor-manager

explanation.definitionFit: A pine is a coniferous plant of the woods, and Sir Herbert Beerbohm bore the surname as an actor.

clue.text: Girlfriend seen in the morning, or at beginning of afternoon

parts.note: taken as written
AM, ante meridiem, is the morning
taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: beginning of picks the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A lover glimpsed in the morning or just after lunch.
explanation.definitionFit: An inamorata is a female lover, a slightly literary word for a girlfriend.

clue.text: Scent of love gloomy

parts.note: love is nil in tennis, the letter O
dour means sullen or gloomy

explanation.surface: A melancholy perfume called love.
explanation.definitionFit: A smell or aroma, a near synonym for scent.

clue.text: Brunel's "Great" ship was English to its end

parts.note: astern means towards the stern, the back end of a ship

explanation.surface: A remark about Isambard Kingdom Brunel's great steamship being English through and through.
explanation.walkthrough: Brunel's giant Victorian steamship was the Great Eastern, so the word after 'Great' is the answer. 'to its end' looks like 'thoroughly'.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous iron steamship built by Isambard Kingdom Brunel was named the Great Eastern.

clue.text: One producing ink endlessly put in before title

indicators.note: put in places one piece inside another

parts.note: ere is an old word for before

indicators.note: endlessly removes the final letter of the word

parts.note: a squid squirts ink

explanation.surface: Something about a pen, refilled endlessly, placed in front of a heading.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' drops only the final letter here; 'title' is the definition, since this courtesy title follows a man's name on an envelope.
explanation.definitionFit: Esquire is a courtesy title written after a man's name in formal address.

clue.text: Block in sport

definitions.meaning: a building block of baked clay
a sport is a good, reliable person, as is a good egg

explanation.definitionFit: A rectangular building block, and in old British slang a stout-hearted fellow or good sport.

clue.text: Unusual if judge backed during depression

indicators.note: during places these letters within the depression

parts.note: a dent is a hollow or depression
taken as written

indicators.note: backed means turned back to front

parts.note: a ref, short for referee, judges a match

explanation.surface: An odd situation: if a judge had support while in a slump.
explanation.walkthrough: 'depression' looks like low spirits, but it is a physical hollow in a surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unusual is unlike the norm, so different is a close synonym.

clue.text: Small vessels assisted me at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A sailor recalls getting help aboard ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Demitasses are small coffee cups, vessels for drinking.

clue.text: 3 crash, fumbling for the soap

indicators.note: fumbling suggests a clumsy mix-up of letters

parts.note: the number three spelt out

explanation.surface: Three crashes as someone fumbles for the bar of soap.
explanation.walkthrough: THE ARCHERS is a long-running BBC radio soap opera about country folk. '3' looks like a cross-reference to 3 Down, but is simply the number.
explanation.definitionFit: A British radio soap opera set in a farming village, broadcast since 1951.

clue.text: Hairy beast collecting dinner, perhaps, saw mouth ulcer as revolting

indicators.note: revolting means in revolt, turning over, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A shaggy animal gathering a meal and finding a mouth sore disgusting.
explanation.walkthrough: The hairy beast is a big drooping moustache, which can catch bits of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A thick drooping moustache, named after a tusked sea mammal, is a hairy thing that traps crumbs.

clue.text: "On the expensive side" has me put off about something built ages ago

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes round another
off means wrong or awry, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: Noah's ark, built in ancient times

explanation.surface: Something pricey that is deterred by ancient construction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put' belongs to the jumbled letters, not to the signal; 'off' alone signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Upmarket means aimed at wealthier buyers, hence costly.

clue.text: Hardened supporter Spike won't start to accept John (not a Tory)

indicators.note: to accept means to take another piece inside
the word loses its first letter

parts.note: an icicle is a spike of ice

indicators.note: not means the following words are removed

parts.note: john is slang for a toilet or lavatory
taken as written, a Conservative

explanation.surface: A political jibe about a tough backer called Spike and a non-Conservative John.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spike' looks like a name but is an icicle; 'John' is slang for a toilet; 'a Tory' is cut from the longer word, leaving the short British slang form.
explanation.definitionFit: The collarbone, a bone being a hard structure that supports the body.

clue.text: Proper order needed to secure Labour's retreat to "The Ride of the Valkyries", possibly?

definitions.text: The Ride of the Valkyries", possibly

indicators.note: retreat means going back, so the whole string is read backwards

parts.note: fit means proper or suitable
OM is the Order of Merit
to tie is to secure
L is the abbreviation for Labour

explanation.surface: Political talk of restoring order to cover Labour's withdrawal, with Wagner playing.
explanation.walkthrough: FIT, OM, TIE and L are read backwards as a whole.
explanation.definitionFit: Wagner gave recurring musical themes to people and ideas; The Ride of the Valkyries uses one example.

clue.text: Spike the demon drink

parts.note: an imp is a small demon
ale is a drink, beer

explanation.surface: Lacing the devil's drink.
explanation.definitionFit: To impale is to pierce with a stake or spike.

clue.text: Sound of disgust voiced for leader

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Sound of disgust voiced for leader (5)' for BLAIR: no sound of disgust is a homophone of BLAIR; BLARE fits 'Sound' alone and leaves 'of disgust' with no job.
annotationWithheld.clue: Sound of disgust voiced for leader

clue.text: Note cow's on the phone!

parts.note: B is a musical note
cow's reads as cow is; a cow lows, so it is a lower

explanation.surface: A scribbled message saying the cow is calling.
explanation.walkthrough: BLOWER is British slang for the telephone.
explanation.definitionFit: Blower is an old British slang word for the telephone.

clue.text: Old script sees old man with loose syrup

parts.note: pa, a father, is one's old man

indicators.note: loose means let free, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An ancient manuscript shows Dad with spilt syrup.
explanation.definitionFit: Ancient writing was set down on papyrus, so the word stands for an old document.

clue.text: Poet makes another hold his head

indicators.note: hold means grip inside, so one piece goes within

parts.note: Edgar Allan Poe is another poet
the first letter of the poet's name

explanation.surface: One poet holding another's head.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexander Pope was an eighteenth-century English poet.

clue.text: Studious lad not entirely reasonable?

indicators.note: the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a boy is a lad
okish means fairly reasonable

explanation.surface: A question about whether a scholarly youngster is quite sensible.
explanation.definitionFit: Bookish means fond of reading and study, so studious.

clue.text: Smile offers support

explanation.definitionFit: A broad grin, and a horizontal timber or girder holding up a structure.

clue.text: Before settlement, but only 20%, yours truly not given a bean!

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Before settlement, but only 20%, yours truly not given a bean! (5)' for PULSE: 'a bean' defines it, but no parse of the rest gives PUL before SE (20% of settlement) or any other split.
annotationWithheld.clue: Before settlement, but only 20%, yours truly not given a bean!

clue.text: Dickens' Sam's heading off to entertain famous person, one putting coat on

indicators.note: to entertain means to take in, so one piece goes inside another
the word loses its first letter

parts.note: Sam Weller is Mr Pickwick's servant in Dickens
a name is a celebrity

explanation.surface: Dickens's Sam Weller setting off to host a celebrity.
explanation.walkthrough: Sam Weller, Mr Pickwick's cockney servant in The Pickwick Papers, is the Dickens character; 'famous person' is a big name.
explanation.definitionFit: An enameller applies a coat of enamel to metal or pottery.
